    def ConstraintAwareRepairAndOptimize(self, candidate_routes, problem):
        # A variant that uses best-improvement 2-opt per-route and global best inter-route moves
        # (single-customer relocate, short-chain relocate up to length 2, and single-customer swap).
        # It applies one best move per iteration (greedy best-improvement) to get stronger changes per step.
        routes = [list(r) for r in candidate_routes if r]
        if not routes:
            return []

        # Ensure capacity constraints first (split oversized routes if needed)
        routes = self.repair_and_split_routes(routes)

        dist = self.distance_matrix
        demands = self.demands
        capacity = self.vehicle_capacity
        depot = self.depot
        EPS = 1e-9

        # Helper: compute route cost
        def compute_cost(r):
            c = 0.0
            for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
                c += dist[a][b]
            return c

        # Helper: route load (excluding depot)
        def route_load(r):
            return sum(demands[x] for x in r if x != depot)

        # Initialize
        routes = [r[:] for r in routes]
        route_costs = [compute_cost(r) for r in routes]
        loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]

        # Parameters
        max_iterations = 40
        max_chain = 2  # allow relocating sequences of length 1..max_chain
        improved = True
        iteration = 0

        while improved and iteration < max_iterations:
            iteration += 1
            improved = False

            R = len(routes)
            # 1) Per-route best-improvement 2-opt
            best_2opt = (0.0, None)  # (delta, (route_idx, i, j))
            for idx, r in enumerate(routes):
                n = len(r)
                if n <= 3:
                    continue
                best_local_delta = 0.0
                best_local_pos = None
                # evaluate all i<j pairs (skipping depot at 0 and n-1)
                for i in range(1, n - 2):
                    a = r[i - 1]
                    b = r[i]
                    for j in range(i + 1, n - 1):
                        c = r[j]
                        d = r[j + 1]
                        delta = dist[a][c] + dist[b][d] - dist[a][b] - dist[c][d]
                        if delta < best_local_delta - EPS:
                            best_local_delta = delta
                            best_local_pos = (i, j)
                if best_local_pos is not None and best_local_delta < best_2opt[0] - EPS:
                    best_2opt = (best_local_delta, (idx, best_local_pos[0], best_local_pos[1]))

            # If a beneficial 2-opt exists, apply it (single best improvement)
            if best_2opt[1] is not None and best_2opt[0] < -EPS:
                delta, (rid, i, j) = best_2opt
                routes[rid][i:j+1] = routes[rid][i:j+1][::-1]
                route_costs[rid] += delta
                improved = True
                # update loads unaffected
                continue  # go to next iteration to re-evaluate (strong greedy move)

            # 2) Global best inter-route moves: relocation (chain up to length max_chain) and swaps (single-customer)
            best_move = (0.0, None)  # (delta, move_descriptor)
            # relocation: remove sequence from r_from at pos length L and insert into r_to at ins
            for i in range(R):
                r_from = routes[i]
                if len(r_from) <= 3:
                    continue
                for pos in range(1, len(r_from) - 1):
                    # consider chains of length 1..max_chain within bounds
                    for L in range(1, max_chain + 1):
                        end_pos = pos + L - 1
                        if end_pos >= len(r_from) - 1:
                            break
                        seq = r_from[pos:end_pos+1]
                        demand_seq = sum(demands[v] for v in seq)
                        a = r_from[pos - 1]
                        b = r_from[end_pos + 1]
                        # removal delta: detach seq and connect a-b
                        # removal cost: -(a->v1 + internal + vk->b) + (a->b)
                        internal_removal = 0.0
                        if L >= 2:
                            for t in range(L - 1):
                                internal_removal += dist[seq[t]][seq[t+1]]
                        removal_delta = - (dist[a][seq[0]] + internal_removal + dist[seq[-1]][b]) + dist[a][b]

                        for j in range(R):
                            if i == j:
                                continue
                            if loads[j] + demand_seq > capacity:
                                continue
                            r_to = routes[j]
                            # try all insertion positions in r_to
                            for ins in range(1, len(r_to)):
                                u = r_to[ins - 1]
                                w = r_to[ins]
                                # insertion delta: (u->v1 + internal + vk->w) - (u->w)
                                insert_delta = dist[u][seq[0]] + internal_removal + dist[seq[-1]][w] - dist[u][w]
                                total_delta = removal_delta + insert_delta
                                if total_delta < best_move[0] - EPS:
                                    best_move = (total_delta, ("relocate_chain", i, pos, end_pos, j, ins, demand_seq))
            # swaps: single-customer swap between two routes
            for i in range(R):
                r_i = routes[i]
                if len(r_i) <= 3:
                    continue
                for j in range(i+1, R):
                    r_j = routes[j]
                    if len(r_j) <= 3:
                        continue
                    # try swapping single customers at positions pi and pj
                    for pi in range(1, len(r_i) - 1):
                        vi = r_i[pi]
                        di = demands[vi]
                        for pj in range(1, len(r_j) - 1):
                            vj = r_j[pj]
                            dj = demands[vj]
                            # capacity feasibility after swap
                            if loads[i] - di + dj > capacity or loads[j] - dj + di > capacity:
                                continue
                            # delta for removing vi and inserting vj at pi in r_i
                            ai = r_i[pi - 1]
                            bi = r_i[pi + 1]
                            remove_i = - (dist[ai][vi] + dist[vi][bi]) + dist[ai][bi]
                            insert_i = dist[ai][vj] + dist[vj][bi] - dist[ai][bi]
                            delta_i = remove_i + insert_i
                            # delta for removing vj and inserting vi at pj in r_j
                            aj = r_j[pj - 1]
                            bj = r_j[pj + 1]
                            remove_j = - (dist[aj][vj] + dist[vj][bj]) + dist[aj][bj]
                            insert_j = dist[aj][vi] + dist[vi][bj] - dist[aj][bj]
                            delta_j = remove_j + insert_j
                            total_delta = delta_i + delta_j
                            if total_delta < best_move[0] - EPS:
                                best_move = (total_delta, ("swap_single", i, pi, j, pj))

            # If a beneficial inter-route move found, apply the best one
            if best_move[1] is not None and best_move[0] < -EPS:
                delta, desc = best_move
                if desc[0] == "relocate_chain":
                    _, i, pos, end_pos, j, ins, demand_seq = desc
                    seq = routes[i][pos:end_pos+1]
                    # insert into r_to at ins
                    routes[j][ins:ins] = seq
                    # remove from r_from (careful if i < j removal index correct because lists separate)
                    # If i == j would be handled differently but we ensured i!=j
                    del routes[i][pos:end_pos+1]
                    loads[i] -= demand_seq
                    loads[j] += demand_seq
                    route_costs[i] = compute_cost(routes[i])
                    route_costs[j] = compute_cost(routes[j])
                    improved = True
                elif desc[0] == "swap_single":
                    _, i, pi, j, pj = desc
                    vi = routes[i][pi]
                    vj = routes[j][pj]
                    # swap elements
                    routes[i][pi], routes[j][pj] = vj, vi
                    # update loads (unchanged)
                    route_costs[i] = compute_cost(routes[i])
                    route_costs[j] = compute_cost(routes[j])
                    improved = True

                # After move, drop degenerate routes (only depot or empty)
                new_routes = []
                for r in routes:
                    if len(r) > 2:
                        new_routes.append(r)
                routes = new_routes
                # Recompute loads and costs to be safe
                route_costs = [compute_cost(r) for r in routes]
                loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
                continue  # next iteration to search for further improvements

            # If reached here, no improving 2-opt or inter-route move found
            break

        # Final cleanup: apply a focused 2-opt per route using provided helper and return valid routes
        final_routes = []
        for r in routes:
            if len(r) > 2:
                improved_route = self._two_opt_route(r)
                final_routes.append(improved_route)
        return final_routes

    def _two_opt_route(self, route):
        dist = self.distance_matrix
        best = list(route)
        improved = True
        while improved:
            improved = False
            n = len(best)
            for i in range(1, n - 2):
                for j in range(i+1, n - 1):
                    newr = best[:i] + best[i:j+1][::-1] + best[j+1:]
                    if self._route_cost(newr) + 1e-9 < self._route_cost(best):
                        best = newr
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:
                    break
        return best

    def _route_cost(self, r):
        if not r or len(r) < 2:
            return 0.0
        s = 0.0
        for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
            s += self.distance_matrix[a][b]
        return s

    def LearnFromMerge(self, mergeModel, cache, candidate):
        # simple heuristic: reward merges that decreased cost - store counts (placeholder)
        # mergeModel is a dict of frozenset->weight; we increment weights for blocks present in candidate
        for route in candidate:
            key = frozenset([v for v in route if v != self.depot])
            if not key:
                continue
            mergeModel['weights'][key] += 1

    def AdaptPartitionScheme(self, partitions, candidate, mergeModel):
        # If some partition contains many cross-route nodes, split it further; otherwise sometimes merge small adjacent ones
        # Simple heuristic: split largest partition if candidate routes indicate it's mixed
        if not partitions:
            return partitions
        sizes = [p['size'] for p in partitions]
        max_idx = int(np.argmax(sizes))
        if sizes[max_idx] > 8:
            # split it
            new_blocks = self.Split(partitions[max_idx], None, mergeModel)
            new_partitions = partitions[:max_idx] + new_blocks + partitions[max_idx+1:]
            return new_partitions
        # sometimes randomly merge two smallest
        if random.random() < 0.1 and len(partitions) >= 2:
            idxs = sorted(range(len(partitions)), key=lambda i: partitions[i]['size'])[:2]
            a = partitions[idxs[0]]['nodes']
            b = partitions[idxs[1]]['nodes']
            merged = {'nodes': frozenset(set(a) | set(b)), 'sig': frozenset(set(a) | set(b)), 'size': len(a) + len(b)}
            new_partitions = [p for k, p in enumerate(partitions) if k not in idxs]
            new_partitions.append(merged)
            return new_partitions
        return partitions

    def IsBetter(self, candidate, best, problem):
        # Compare total cost; lower is better
        def cost_of(sol_routes):
            return sum(self._route_cost(r) for r in sol_routes)
        if best is None:
            return True
        return cost_of(candidate) + 1e-9 < cost_of(best)

    def DecodeSolution(self, best, problem):
        # flatten routes into required list format
        flat = []
        for r in best:
            if not r:
                continue
            if flat and flat[-1] == self.depot:

                pass
            # ensure route starts with depot
            if r[0] != self.depot:
                r = [self.depot] + r
            if r[-1] != self.depot:
                r = r + [self.depot]
            flat.extend(r)
        # ensure starts and ends with depot and customers appear once
        if not flat:
            return [self.depot, self.depot]
        if flat[0] != self.depot:
            flat = [self.depot] + flat
        if flat[-1] != self.depot:
            flat = flat + [self.depot]
        # final check: every customer exactly once; if missing, append their own route
        customers = set(range(1, self.n))

                continue
            cleaned.append(x)
        # ensure last is depot
        if cleaned[-1] != self.depot:
            cleaned.append(self.depot)
        return cleaned

    # --- main solver implementing RECURSIVE_PARTITION_MERGE ---
    def solve(self) -> list:

import time
import itertools
import random
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict

class FSSPSolver:
    def __init__(self, num_jobs: int, num_machines: int, processing_times: list):
        """
        Initialize the FSSP solver.

        Args:
            num_jobs: Number of jobs in the problem
            num_machines: Number of machines in the problem
            processing_times: List of lists where processing_times[j][m] is the processing time of job j on machine m
        """
        self.num_jobs = num_jobs
        self.num_machines = num_machines
        self.processing_times = np.array(processing_times)
        # Precompute job total times for heuristics
        self.job_totals = np.sum(self.processing_times, axis=1)

    # ----------------- Helper functions -----------------
    def _makespan(self, sequence: List[int]) -> float:
        """Compute makespan (C_max) of a sequence on the flow shop."""
        if not sequence:
            return 0.0
        m = self.num_machines
        machine_times = np.zeros(m, dtype=float)
        for job in sequence:
            prev_finish = 0.0
            for k in range(m):
                start = max(machine_times[k], prev_finish)
                finish = start + self.processing_times[job, k]
                machine_times[k] = finish
                prev_finish = finish
        return float(machine_times[-1])

    def _neh_construct(self, jobs: List[int]) -> Tuple[List[int], float]:
        """NEH heuristic for a given subset of jobs."""
        # Order by descending total processing time
        ordered = sorted(jobs, key=lambda j: -self.job_totals[j])
        seq = []
        best_seq = []
        best_mk = float('inf')
        for j in ordered:
            # insert job j into best position in seq
            best_local_seq = None
            best_local_mk = float('inf')
            for pos in range(len(seq) + 1):
                candidate = seq[:pos] + [j] + seq[pos:]
                mk = self._makespan(candidate)
                if mk < best_local_mk:
                    best_local_mk = mk
                    best_local_seq = candidate
            seq = best_local_seq
            if best_local_mk < best_mk:
                best_mk = best_local_mk
                best_seq = seq[:]
        if not best_seq:
            best_seq = seq[:]
            best_mk = self._makespan(best_seq)
        return best_seq, best_mk

    def _exact_solve(self, jobs: List[int]) -> Tuple[List[int], float]:
        """Brute-force exact solver for very small blocks (permutations)."""
        best_seq = None
        best_mk = float('inf')
        for perm in itertools.permutations(jobs):
            mk = self._makespan(list(perm))
            if mk < best_mk:
                best_mk = mk
                best_seq = list(perm)
        return best_seq, best_mk

    def _block_key(self, jobs: List[int]) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
        """Key for caching a block: sorted tuple"""
        return tuple(sorted(jobs))

    # ----------------- Partition & merge utilities -----------------
    def _initial_partition(self, budget_seconds: float) -> List[List[int]]:
        """Create initial balanced partitions by sorting jobs by total time and chunking."""
        n = self.num_jobs
        # Block size roughly sqrt(n) but at least 2
        block_size = max(2, int(max(2, np.sqrt(max(1, n)))))
        # sort jobs by total processing time descending
        sorted_jobs = sorted(range(n), key=lambda j: -self.job_totals[j])
        partitions = [sorted_jobs[i:i+block_size] for i in range(0, n, block_size)]
        return partitions

    def _split_block(self, block: List[int], merge_model: np.ndarray) -> List[List[int]]:
        """Split a block into two subblocks. Use preference info if available, else split by median total."""
        if len(block) <= 2:
            return [block]
        # Try to use merge_model preferences to cluster: spectral-like by principal eigenvector of submatrix
        try:
            subm = merge_model[np.ix_(block, block)]
            # Row sums reflect tendency to be early
            scores = np.sum(subm, axis=1)
            idx_sorted = np.argsort(-scores)  # higher score earlier
            ordered = [block[i] for i in idx_sorted]
        except Exception:
            ordered = sorted(block, key=lambda j: -self.job_totals[j])
        mid = len(ordered) // 2
        return [ordered[:mid], ordered[mid:]]

    def _merge_order_blocks(self, subblocks: List[List[int]], cache: Dict[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[List[int], float]], merge_model: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[List[int], float]:
        """Decide an ordering of subblocks and concatenate cached sequences. If few blocks, try permutations."""
        k = len(subblocks)
        # prepare sequences and makespans from cache
        seqs = []
        for b in subblocks:
            key = self._block_key(b)
            if key in cache:
                seqs.append(cache[key][0])
            else:
                # fallback: NEH on block
                s, _ = self._neh_construct(b)
                seqs.append(s)
        # If small number of blocks, try all permutations
        best_seq = None
        best_mk = float('inf')
        if k <= 6:
            for perm_idx in itertools.permutations(range(k)):
                candidate = []
                for idx in perm_idx:
                    candidate.extend(seqs[idx])
                mk = self._makespan(candidate)
                if mk < best_mk:
                    best_mk = mk
                    best_seq = candidate
            return best_seq, best_mk
        # Otherwise, greedy order by average preference score between blocks (higher earlier)
        block_scores = []
        for i, b in enumerate(subblocks):
            # score = average preference of jobs in b to be before other jobs
            members = np.array(b, dtype=int)
            score = np.sum(merge_model[np.ix_(members, np.arange(self.num_jobs))])  # larger => tends to be before others
            block_scores.append((score, i))
        block_scores.sort(reverse=True)
        ordered_seq = []
        for _, idx in block_scores:
            ordered_seq.extend(seqs[idx])
        return ordered_seq, self._makespan(ordered_seq)

    # ----------------- Local search / repair -----------------
    def _local_search_improve(self, sequence: List[int], time_budget: float) -> Tuple[List[int], float]:
        """Simple local search: adjacent swap and random pair swap hill-climbing within time_budget seconds."""
        start = time.time()
        best_seq = sequence[:]
        best_mk = self._makespan(best_seq)
        n = len(sequence)
        improved = True
        # First do steepest adjacent swap passes
        while improved and (time.time() - start) < time_budget:
            improved = False
            for i in range(n - 1):
                s = best_seq[:]
                s[i], s[i+1] = s[i+1], s[i]
                mk = self._makespan(s)
                if mk < best_mk - 1e-9:
                    best_mk = mk
                    best_seq = s
                    improved = True
                    break
        # Then random pair swaps until time out
        while (time.time() - start) < time_budget:
            i, j = random.randrange(0, n), random.randrange(0, n)
            if i == j:
                continue
            s = best_seq[:]
            s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
            mk = self._makespan(s)
            if mk < best_mk - 1e-9:
                best_mk = mk
                best_seq = s
        return best_seq, best_mk

    # ----------------- Main recursive procedure -----------------
    def solve(self) -> list:
        """
        Solve the Flow Shop Scheduling Problem (FSSP).

        Returns:
            A list representing the sequence of jobs to be processed.
        """
        # Set time budget proportional to problem size (seconds)
        budget_seconds = min(30.0, max(1.0, 0.02 * self.num_jobs * max(1, self.num_machines)))
        start_time = time.time()

        # Analyze structure -> trivial signature (job totals)
        # Initialize merge_model as preference counts: jobs x jobs, higher means job i tends to be before j
        merge_model = np.zeros((self.num_jobs, self.num_jobs), dtype=float)

        # Initial partitions
        partitions = self._initial_partition(budget_seconds)

        cache: Dict[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[List[int], float]] = {}

        # Helper recursive solver for subblocks
        def solve_block(block: List[int]):
            key = self._block_key(block)
            if key in cache:
                return cache[key]
            # If block small enough, use exact solver
            if len(block) <= 7:
                seq, mk = self._exact_solve(block)
                cache[key] = (seq, mk)
                return cache[key]
            # Otherwise split and solve recursively
            subblocks = self._split_block(block, merge_model)
            # Solve each subblock
            for sb in subblocks:
                solve_block(sb)
            # Merge cached subblocks
            merged_seq, merged_mk = self._merge_order_blocks(subblocks, cache, merge_model)
            # Local optimize merged sequence (small time slice)
            time_left = max(0.01, budget_seconds * 0.005)
            merged_seq, merged_mk = self._local_search_improve(merged_seq, time_left)
            cache[key] = (merged_seq, merged_mk)
            return cache[key]

        # Baseline candidate using NEH on full set
        all_jobs = list(range(self.num_jobs))
        best_seq, best_mk = self._neh_construct(all_jobs)
        best_candidate = (best_seq, best_mk)

        # Main loop until time budget exhausted
        iteration = 0
        while (time.time() - start_time) < budget_seconds:
            iteration += 1
            # Process partitions: ensure each partition has cached solution
            for block in partitions:
                key = self._block_key(block)
                if key in cache:
                    continue
                if len(block) <= 7:
                    seq, mk = self._exact_solve(block)
                    cache[key] = (seq, mk)
                else:
                    # split and solve recursively
                    subblocks = self._split_block(block, merge_model)
                    for sb in subblocks:
                        solve_block(sb)
                    merged_seq, merged_mk = self._merge_order_blocks(subblocks, cache, merge_model)
                    # slight local search
                    time_slice = max(0.005, budget_seconds * 0.002)
                    merged_seq, merged_mk = self._local_search_improve(merged_seq, time_slice)
                    cache[key] = (merged_seq, merged_mk)

            # Assemble from cache (order partitions)
            assemble_seq, assemble_mk = self._merge_order_blocks(partitions, cache, merge_model)
            # Repair & optimize (full local search for candidate)
            remaining_time = max(0.01, budget_seconds * 0.02)
            assemble_seq, assemble_mk = self._local_search_improve(assemble_seq, remaining_time)

            # Learn from this candidate: update pairwise precedence counts
            for i_idx, i_job in enumerate(assemble_seq):
                for j_job in assemble_seq[i_idx+1:]:
                    merge_model[i_job, j_job] += 1.0

            # Adapt partitions: if candidate improved, try merging small adjacent partitions; else split largest partition
            if assemble_mk < best_candidate[1] - 1e-9:
                best_candidate = (assemble_seq, assemble_mk)
                # merge small adjacent partitions to try exploit
                if len(partitions) >= 2:
                    # merge two smallest partitions
                    sizes = [(len(p), idx) for idx, p in enumerate(partitions)]
                    sizes.sort()
                    _, idx1 = sizes[0]
                    _, idx2 = sizes[1] if len(sizes) > 1 else (None, None)
                    if idx2 is not None:
                        # merge them
                        new_partitions = []
                        merged_flag = False
                        for idx, p in enumerate(partitions):
                            if idx == idx1:
                                continue
                            if idx == idx2 and not merged_flag:
                                new_partitions.append(partitions[idx1] + partitions[idx2])
                                merged_flag = True
                            elif idx != idx1:
                                new_partitions.append(p)
                        partitions = new_partitions
            else:
                # split the largest partition to escape local optima
                largest_idx = max(range(len(partitions)), key=lambda i: len(partitions[i]))
                if len(partitions[largest_idx]) > 2:
                    new_subs = self._split_block(partitions[largest_idx], merge_model)
                    partitions = partitions[:largest_idx] + new_subs + partitions[largest_idx+1:]

            # update global best
            if assemble_mk < best_mk - 1e-9:
                best_seq, best_mk = assemble_seq, assemble_mk

            # termination guard for small remaining time
            if (time.time() - start_time) > budget_seconds * 0.95:
                break

        # Final decode solution: ensure permutation of all jobs
        # If best_seq missing some jobs (shouldn't), fill with remaining jobs using NEH
        final_seq = best_seq[:]
        missing = [j for j in range(self.num_jobs) if j not in final_seq]
        if missing:
            # insert missing jobs with NEH-style insertion
            for j in missing:
                best_local_seq = None
                best_local_mk = float('inf')
                for pos in range(len(final_seq)+1):
                    cand = final_seq[:pos] + [j] + final_seq[pos:]
                    mk = self._makespan(cand)
                    if mk < best_local_mk:
                        best_local_mk = mk
                        best_local_seq = cand
                final_seq = best_local_seq

        return final_seq

# Your key function here
def two_opt(self, tour: List[int], time_limit_seconds: float = 0.05) -> List[int]:
    """
    Optimized 2-opt local search (first-improvement) with tighter inner-loop bookkeeping
    and micro-optimizations to reduce attribute lookups and Python overhead.
    """
    start_time = time.time()
    if not tour:
        return tour
    n = len(tour)
    if n <= 2:
        return tour
    # Local bindings to avoid repeated attribute lookups
    mat = self.distance_matrix
    best = tour[:]  # operate on a copy
    best_cost = 0.0
    # compute initial cost
    for i in range(n):
        a = best[i]
        b = best[(i + 1) % n]
        best_cost += mat[a, b]
    # 2-opt first-improvement loop with time check
    improved = True
    time_check = time.time
    # Pre-allocate some variables to reduce name lookups in loops
    while improved and (time_check() - start_time) < time_limit_seconds:
        improved = False
        # iterate over possible i (edge (i,i+1))
        # we stop at n-2 because j must be at least i+2
        for i in range(n - 2):
            a = best[i]
            b = best[i + 1]
            # choose j range: if i == 0, cannot choose j == n-1 (would be same edge)
            j_start = i + 2
            j_end = n - 1 if i > 0 else n - 2
            # inner loop: try to find first improving j
            for j in range(j_start, j_end + 1):
                c = best[j]
                d = best[(j + 1) % n]
                # compute gain: remove (a-b) and (c-d), add (a-c) and (b-d)
                delta = (mat[a, c] + mat[b, d]) - (mat[a, b] + mat[c, d])
                if delta < -1e-12:
                    # perform 2-opt reversal of segment (i+1 .. j)
                    # slice reversal is efficient in practice and implemented in C
                    best[i + 1 : j + 1] = reversed(best[i + 1 : j + 1])
                    best_cost += delta
                    improved = True
                    break  # first-improvement: restart outer scan
            if improved or (time_check() - start_time) >= time_limit_seconds:
                break
    return best

# Your key function here
def ConstraintAwareRepairAndOptimize(self, candidate_routes, problem):
    # Local search: efficient 2-opt per route and relocate between routes to reduce cost and ensure capacity
    # Optimized to use incremental delta evaluations and early exits.
    routes = [list(r) for r in candidate_routes if r]
    if not routes:
        return []

    # First ensure capacity constraints by splitting oversized routes
    routes = self.repair_and_split_routes(routes)

    dist = self.distance_matrix
    demands = self.demands
    capacity = self.vehicle_capacity
    depot = self.depot
    EPS = 1e-9

    # Helper: compute route cost
    def compute_cost(r):
        c = 0.0
        for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
            c += dist[a][b]
        return c

    # Initialize route costs and loads
    route_costs = [compute_cost(r) for r in routes]
    loads = [sum(demands[x] for x in r if x != depot) for r in routes]

    # Fast 2-opt using delta evaluations per route
    for idx, r in enumerate(routes):
        # Skip trivial routes
        if len(r) <= 3:
            continue
        improved = True
        while improved:
            improved = False
            n = len(r)
            # i from 1..n-3, j from i+1..n-2 (since r[0] and r[-1] are depots)
            for i in range(1, n - 2):
                a = r[i - 1]
                b = r[i]
                # inner j loop
                for j in range(i + 1, n - 1):
                    c = r[j]
                    d = r[j + 1]
                    # delta for reversing segment [i..j]
                    delta = dist[a][c] + dist[b][d] - dist[a][b] - dist[c][d]
                    if delta < -EPS:
                        # perform reversal
                        r[i:j+1] = r[i:j+1][::-1]
                        route_costs[idx] += delta
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:
                    break

    # Relocate moves between routes (single-customer moves), improved with incremental updates
    max_iterations = 10
    iteration = 0
    improved = True
    while improved and iteration < max_iterations:
        iteration += 1
        improved = False
        # Recompute loads and costs to be safe
        loads = [sum(demands[x] for x in r if x != depot) for r in routes]
        route_costs = [compute_cost(r) for r in routes]
        R = len(routes)
        # Try relocating from any route to any other route
        outer_break = False
        for i in range(R):
            if outer_break:
                break
            r_from = routes[i]
            if len(r_from) <= 3:
                continue  # nothing to move (only depot + one customer or empty)
            for j in range(R):
                if i == j:
                    continue
                r_to = routes[j]
                # Pre-check capacity feasibility: we will check per-customer
                for pos in range(1, len(r_from) - 1):
                    v = r_from[pos]
                    demand_v = demands[v]
                    if loads[j] + demand_v > capacity:
                        continue
                    # delta from removal in r_from
                    a = r_from[pos - 1]
                    b = r_from[pos + 1]
                    removal_delta = - (dist[a][v] + dist[v][b]) + dist[a][b]
                    best_delta = 0.0
                    best_ins = None
                    # try best insertion position in r_to
                    # positions 1..len(r_to)-1
                    for ins in range(1, len(r_to)):
                        u = r_to[ins - 1]
                        w = r_to[ins]
                        insert_delta = dist[u][v] + dist[v][w] - dist[u][w]
                        delta = removal_delta + insert_delta
                        if delta < best_delta - EPS:
                            best_delta = delta
                            best_ins = ins
                    if best_ins is not None:
                        # perform the move: insert into r_to at best_ins, remove from r_from at pos
                        # Important: when i < j and we modify r_from first, indices of r_to unaffected because different lists
                        routes[j].insert(best_ins, v)
                        del routes[i][pos]
                        # update loads and costs
                        loads[i] -= demand_v
                        loads[j] += demand_v
                        route_costs[i] += removal_delta
                        route_costs[j] += (best_delta - removal_delta)  # equals insert_delta
                        improved = True
                        outer_break = True
                        break
                if outer_break:
                    break
            if outer_break:
                break
        # After a move, remove any degenerate routes (length <= 2)
        if improved:
            new_routes = []
            for r in routes:
                if len(r) > 2:
                    new_routes.append(r)
            routes = new_routes
            # Recompute costs and loads for next iteration
            route_costs = [compute_cost(r) for r in routes]
            loads = [sum(demands[x] for x in r if x != depot) for r in routes]

    # Final cleanup: ensure all routes are valid and apply a final light 2-opt using the optimized per-route function
    final_routes = []
    for r in routes:
        if len(r) > 2:
            # apply a focused 2-opt (reuse _two_opt_route which also uses route cost checks)
            improved_route = self._two_opt_route(r)
            final_routes.append(improved_route)
    return final_routes

# Your key function here
def _makespan(self, sequence: List[int]) -> float:
    """Compute makespan (C_max) of a sequence on the flow shop.
    Optimized implementation:
      - caches a pure-Python nested list view of processing times for fast indexing
      - uses local variables and plain Python lists to avoid numpy overhead in tight loops
    """
    if not sequence:
        return 0.0

    # Lazy cache conversion to Python lists for faster repeated access
    if not hasattr(self, "_pt_list"):
        # convert once; subsequent calls reuse this attribute
        self._pt_list = self.processing_times.tolist()

    pt = self._pt_list  # List[List[float]]
    m = self.num_machines

    # Use a plain Python list for machine completion times (faster than numpy for scalar ops)
    machine_times = [0.0] * m
    range_m = range(m)

    # Tight inner loops with local variables to minimize attribute lookups
    for job in sequence:
        row = pt[job]          # processing times of this job across machines (Python list)
        prev_finish = 0.0
        mt = machine_times
        # iterate by index to update machine_times in place
        for k in range_m:
            # start = max(mt[k], prev_finish) but inline max for speed
            current_machine_ready = mt[k]
            if current_machine_ready > prev_finish:
                start = current_machine_ready
            else:
                start = prev_finish
            finish = start + row[k]
            mt[k] = finish
            prev_finish = finish

    return float(machine_times[-1])

import time
import numpy as np
import copy
from typing import List, Dict, Any

class FSSPSolver:
    def __init__(self, num_jobs: int, num_machines: int, processing_times: list, seed: int = 0):
        """
        Initialize the FSSP solver.

        Args:
            num_jobs: Number of jobs in the problem
            num_machines: Number of machines in the problem
            processing_times: List of lists where processing_times[j][m] is the processing time of job j on machine m
            seed: random seed for reproducibility
        """
        self.num_jobs = int(num_jobs)
        self.num_machines = int(num_machines)
        self.processing_times = np.array(processing_times, dtype=float)
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)

    # --- Utility: cost (makespan) evaluation ---
    def evaluate_makespan(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> float:
        """
        Alternative makespan evaluator for permutation flow-shop.
        Builds the completion time matrix C where
            C[i, j] = processing_time(seq[i], j) + max(C[i-1, j], C[i, j-1])
        and returns C[-1, -1]. Uses numpy indexing to extract the sequence rows
        and a simple double loop to fill the DP table.
        """
        # Handle trivial/empty cases
        # If sequence is empty or no machines, makespan is zero
        try:
            seq_arr = np.asarray(seq, dtype=int)
        except Exception:
            seq_arr = np.array(list(seq), dtype=int)

        k = seq_arr.size
        if k == 0 or getattr(self, "num_machines", 0) == 0:
            return 0.0

        proc_times = self.processing_times  # numpy array shape (num_jobs, num_machines)
        M = int(self.num_machines)

        # Extract only the rows for the given sequence (shape: k x M)
        # This also converts possible numpy scalar types to standard numpy array entries
        job_rows = proc_times[seq_arr]

        # Completion time DP table: C[i, j] is completion time of i-th job in seq on machine j
        C = np.zeros((k, M), dtype=float)

        # Fill first cell
        C[0, 0] = float(job_rows[0, 0])

        # First job across machines (row 0) is cumulative sum
        for j in range(1, M):
            C[0, j] = C[0, j - 1] + float(job_rows[0, j])

        # Remaining jobs
        for i in range(1, k):
            # First machine for job i: previous job completion on machine 0 plus its processing time
            C[i, 0] = C[i - 1, 0] + float(job_rows[i, 0])
            for j in range(1, M):
                # job_rows[i, j] is the processing time for seq[i] on machine j
                pj = float(job_rows[i, j])
                # machine j becomes free at C[i-1, j] (previous job) and job i arrives at C[i, j-1]
                # so start = max(C[i-1, j], C[i, j-1])
                prev_start = C[i - 1, j]
                left = C[i, j - 1]
                if prev_start > left:
                    start = prev_start
                else:
                    start = left
                C[i, j] = start + pj

        return float(C[-1, -1])

    # --- Repair / Validate: ensure a proper permutation ---
    def repair(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        # If seq contains duplicates or misses jobs, repair by filling missing and removing duplicates
        n = self.num_jobs
        seq = seq.astype(int)
        present = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
        out = []
        for x in seq:
            if 0 <= x < n and not present[x]:
                out.append(x)
                present[x] = True
        missing = [i for i in range(n) if not present[i]]
        if missing:
            # append missing items (shuffle to add diversity)
            self.rng.shuffle(missing)
            out.extend(missing)
        return np.array(out, dtype=int)

    # --- Operators ---
    def op_swap(self, seq: np.ndarray, k: int = None) -> np.ndarray:
        a = seq.copy()
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return a
        if k is None:
            i, j = self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False)
        else:
            i = k % n
            j = (i + 1 + (k // n)) % n
        a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
        return a

    def op_insert(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        a = seq.copy().tolist()
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return seq.copy()
        i, j = self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False)
        val = a.pop(i)
        a.insert(j, val)
        return np.array(a, dtype=int)

    def op_reverse_segment(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        a = seq.copy()
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return a
        i, j = sorted(self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False))
        a[i:j+1] = a[i:j+1][::-1]
        return a

    def op_random_shuffle_segment(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        a = seq.copy()
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return a
        i, j = sorted(self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False))
        seg = a[i:j+1].copy()
        self.rng.shuffle(seg)
        a[i:j+1] = seg
        return a

    def op_greedy_insert(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        # take a random job out and reinsert at place minimizing partial makespan increment heuristically
        a = seq.copy().tolist()
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return seq.copy()
        i = self.rng.randint(0, n)
        job = a.pop(i)
        best_pos = 0
        best_cost = float('inf')
        # evaluate placement quickly by local makespan estimate: try limited positions
        positions = list(range(n))
        if n > 10:
            # sample candidate positions to keep cost low
            positions = sorted(self.rng.choice(n, min(10, n), replace=False).tolist() + [0, n-1])
        for pos in positions:
            cand = a[:pos] + [job] + a[pos:]
            cost = self.partial_makespan_estimate(np.array(cand, dtype=int))
            if cost < best_cost:
                best_cost = cost
                best_pos = pos
        a.insert(best_pos, job)
        return np.array(a, dtype=int)

    def partial_makespan_estimate(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> float:
        # approximate makespan by simulating first K jobs or full if small
        return self.evaluate_makespan(seq)

    # --- Local search (adaptive) ---
    def adaptive_local_search(self, seq: np.ndarray, current_cost: float, max_evals: int = 200) -> (np.ndarray, float):
        best_seq = seq.copy()
        best_cost = current_cost
        n = len(seq)
        evals = 0
        # simple first-improvement pairwise swap / insert neighborhood with random sampling
        while evals < max_evals:
            i, j = self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False)
            cand = best_seq.copy()
            cand[i], cand[j] = cand[j], cand[i]
            cand_cost = self.evaluate_makespan(cand)
            evals += 1
            if cand_cost < best_cost:
                best_seq = cand
                best_cost = cand_cost
                # intensify around this improvement
                evals = 0 if evals < max_evals // 4 else evals
            # small chance to try insert
            if self.rng.rand() < 0.1 and evals < max_evals:
                u, v = self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False)
                cand2 = best_seq.tolist()
                val = cand2.pop(u)
                cand2.insert(v, val)
                cand2 = np.array(cand2, dtype=int)
                cand2_cost = self.evaluate_makespan(cand2)
                evals += 1
                if cand2_cost < best_cost:
                    best_seq = cand2
                    best_cost = cand2_cost
        return best_seq, best_cost

    # --- Path relinking ---
    def path_relink(self, src: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, max_steps: int = 50) -> np.ndarray:
        # move src towards target by swapping mispositioned elements one by one
        a = src.copy()
        n = len(a)
        pos_in_a = {int(a[i]): i for i in range(n)}
        steps = 0
        best = a.copy()
        best_cost = self.evaluate_makespan(a)
        for i in range(n):
            if steps >= max_steps:
                break
            if a[i] != target[i]:
                # bring the job that should be at i into position i
                job_needed = int(target[i])
                j = pos_in_a[job_needed]
                a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
                pos_in_a[int(a[j])] = j
                pos_in_a[int(a[i])] = i
                steps += 1
                c = self.evaluate_makespan(a)
                if c < best_cost:
                    best = a.copy()
                    best_cost = c
        return best

    # --- Pool and Elite management ---
    def init_pool(self, pool_size: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        pool = []
        base = np.arange(self.num_jobs, dtype=int)
        for i in range(pool_size):
            seq = base.copy()
            self.rng.shuffle(seq)
            seq = self.repair(seq)
            cost = self.evaluate_makespan(seq)
            pool.append({'seq': seq, 'cost': cost, 'age': 0, 'id': i})
        return pool

    def update_pool_with_candidate(self, pool: List[Dict], cand: Dict, pool_size: int):
        # replace worst if candidate better than worst OR by age-based replacement otherwise
        worst_idx = max(range(len(pool)), key=lambda k: pool[k]['cost'])
        worst_cost = pool[worst_idx]['cost']
        if cand['cost'] < worst_cost or self.rng.rand() < 0.1:
            pool[worst_idx] = cand
        else:
            # sometimes replace a random old element to maintain diversity
            if self.rng.rand() < 0.05:
                idx = self.rng.randint(len(pool))
                pool[idx] = cand

    def maintain_elite(self, elite: List[Dict], candidate: Dict, elite_size: int):
        # insert candidate into elite if good
        elite.append({'seq': candidate['seq'].copy(), 'cost': candidate['cost']})
        elite.sort(key=lambda x: x['cost'])
        # keep unique sequences by cost and content roughly
        kept = []
        seen = set()
        for e in elite:
            key = tuple(e['seq'].tolist())
            if key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                kept.append(e)
            if len(kept) >= elite_size:
                break
        return kept

    # --- Decomposition (multi-scale) ---
    def multi_scale_decompose(self, pool: List[Dict], elite: List[Dict], scales: int = 3):
        # create candidate focuses as contiguous segments of sequences across pool members
        focuses = []
        n = self.num_jobs
        for _ in range(min(len(pool), 10)):
            member = pool[self.rng.randint(len(pool))]
            seq = member['seq']
            # pick scale: small, medium, large
            scale = self.rng.choice(scales)
            seg_len = max(1, n // (2 ** scale))
            i = self.rng.randint(0, max(1, n - seg_len + 1))
            block = seq[i:i+seg_len].copy()
            focuses.append({'block': block, 'start': i, 'length': seg_len, 'embedding': None})
        return focuses

    # --- Contextual bandit selection for operators (UCB-like) ---
    def select_operator(self, op_stats: Dict[str, Dict], total_count: int, exploration: float = 1.0) -> str:
        # op_stats[name] = {'score':float, 'count':int}
        best_name = None
        best_val = -float('inf')
        for name, st in op_stats.items():
            count = max(1, st['count'])
            ucb = st['score'] + exploration * np.sqrt(np.log(max(1, total_count)) / count)
            if ucb > best_val:
                best_val = ucb
                best_name = name
        return best_name

    def update_operator_stats(self, op_stats: Dict[str, Dict], name: str, reward: float):
        s = op_stats[name]
        s['count'] += 1
        # incremental update of average reward
        s['score'] += (reward - s['score']) / s['count']

    # --- Acceptance ---
    def dual_acceptance(self, cand: Dict, pool: List[Dict], elite: List[Dict], memory: Dict) -> Dict:
        # Accept into pool depending on improvement and novelty
        best_pool_cost = min(p['cost'] for p in pool)
        novelty = self.compute_novelty(cand['seq'], pool, elite)
        accept = False
        if cand['cost'] < best_pool_cost:
            accept = True
        else:
            # accept with probability based on novelty and slight chance
            p = min(0.3 + 0.5 * novelty, 0.9)
            accept = (self.rng.rand() < p)
        if accept:
            return cand
        else:
            # degrade candidate to be less aggressive: do minor perturbation
            seq = cand['seq']
            seq = self.op_swap(seq)
            seq = self.repair(seq)
            cand = {'seq': seq, 'cost': self.evaluate_makespan(seq), 'age': 0, 'id': cand.get('id', -1)}
            return cand

    def compute_novelty(self, seq: np.ndarray, pool: List[Dict], elite: List[Dict]) -> float:
        # normalized average Hamming distance to pool + elite
        comps = pool + elite
        if not comps:
            return 1.0
        d_total = 0.0
        for c in comps:
            other = c['seq']
            d_total += np.sum(seq != other) / max(1, len(seq))
        return float(d_total / len(comps))

    # --- Restart and recombine ---
    def restart_and_recombine(self, elite: List[Dict], pool_size: int) -> List[Dict]:
        new_pool = []
        base = np.arange(self.num_jobs, dtype=int)
        # keep some elites and create recombinations
        kept = [e['seq'] for e in elite[:max(1, min(len(elite), pool_size // 4))]]
        # fill pool with recombined elites + random shuffles
        for i in range(pool_size):
            if i < len(kept):
                seq = kept[i].copy()
            elif self.rng.rand() < 0.5 and len(kept) >= 2:
                a, b = self.rng.choice(len(kept), 2, replace=False)
                seq = self.crossover_order(kept[a], kept[b])
            else:
                seq = base.copy()
                self.rng.shuffle(seq)
            seq = self.repair(seq)
            new_pool.append({'seq': seq, 'cost': self.evaluate_makespan(seq), 'age': 0, 'id': i})
        return new_pool

    def crossover_order(self, a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        # Order crossover (OX) simple implementation
        n = len(a)
        if n < 2:
            return a.copy()
        i, j = sorted(self.rng.choice(n, 2, replace=False))
        child = [-1] * n
        child[i:j+1] = a[i:j+1].tolist()
        cur = (j + 1) % n
        for k in range(n):
            idx = (j + 1 + k) % n
            val = b[idx]
            if val not in child:
                child[cur] = int(val)
                cur = (cur + 1) % n
        return np.array(child, dtype=int)

    # --- Main solve implementing the pseudocode structure ---
    def solve(self) -> List[int]:
        if self.num_jobs <= 1:
            return list(range(self.num_jobs))
        # Parameters
        pool_size = max(6, min(40, 2 * self.num_jobs))
        elite_size = max(2, min(10, pool_size // 4))
        max_iters = max(200, 50 * self.num_jobs)
        time_limit = min(30.0, 0.02 * self.num_jobs + 5.0)  # seconds budget heuristic
        start_time = time.time()

        # Initialize memory and operator stats
        memory = {'iter': 0, 'stagnation': 0, 'best_cost': float('inf')}
        operators = {
            'swap': self.op_swap,
            'insert': self.op_insert,
            'reverse': self.op_reverse_segment,
            'shuffle_segment': self.op_random_shuffle_segment,
            'greedy_insert': self.op_greedy_insert
        }
        op_stats = {name: {'score': 0.0, 'count': 0} for name in operators.keys()}

        # Initialize pool and elite
        pool = self.init_pool(pool_size)
        elite = []
        for s in pool:
            elite = self.maintain_elite(elite, s, elite_size)
            if s['cost'] < memory['best_cost']:
                memory['best_cost'] = s['cost']
                memory['best_seq'] = s['seq'].copy()

        # Main loop
        iter_count = 0
        while (time.time() - start_time) < time_limit and iter_count < max_iters:
            iter_count += 1
            memory['iter'] = iter_count
            # Multi-scale decomposition -> focuses
            focuses = self.multi_scale_decompose(pool, elite, scales=3)
            if not focuses:
                focuses = [{'block': np.array([], dtype=int), 'embedding': None}]
            # select a random focus biased by novelty (simple)
            focus = focuses[self.rng.randint(len(focuses))]

            # select parent from pool biased by fitness and age (roulette on inverse cost)
            costs = np.array([p['cost'] for p in pool], dtype=float)
            inv = 1.0 / (1.0 + costs - costs.min())
            probs = inv / inv.sum()
            parent_idx = self.rng.choice(len(pool), p=probs)
            parent = pool[parent_idx]['seq']

            # select operator by contextual bandit (UCB)
            total_ops = sum(st['count'] for st in op_stats.values()) + 1
            op_name = self.select_operator(op_stats, total_ops, exploration=1.5)
            op_func = operators[op_name]

            # operator cascade: apply operator(s), repair, local search
            child_seq = op_func(parent.copy())
            child_seq = self.repair(child_seq)
            child_cost = self.evaluate_makespan(child_seq)
            # adaptive local search limited by problem size
            child_seq, child_cost = self.adaptive_local_search(child_seq, child_cost, max_evals= max(20, 5 * self.num_machines))

            child = {'seq': child_seq, 'cost': child_cost, 'age': 0, 'id': -1}

            # path relink with an elite selected by proximity to focus (if any elite)
            if elite:
                # choose elite by lowest distance
                dists = [np.sum(child_seq != e['seq']) for e in elite]
                elite_choice = elite[int(np.argmin(dists))]['seq']
                child2_seq = self.path_relink(child_seq, elite_choice, max_steps= max(10, self.num_jobs // 5))
                child2_seq = self.repair(child2_seq)
                child2_cost = self.evaluate_makespan(child2_seq)
                child_prime = {'seq': child2_seq, 'cost': child2_cost, 'age': 0, 'id': -1}
            else:
                child_prime = child

            # Evaluate and dual acceptance
            for cand in (child, child_prime):
                cand = cand.copy()
                cand = self.dual_acceptance(cand, pool, elite, memory)
                # update pool and elite
                self.update_pool_with_candidate(pool, cand, pool_size)
                elite = self.maintain_elite(elite, cand, elite_size)
                # operator reward: improvement over parent cost
                parent_cost = pool[parent_idx]['cost']
                reward = max(0.0, parent_cost - cand['cost'])
                self.update_operator_stats(op_stats, op_name, reward)
                # update global best
                if cand['cost'] < memory.get('best_cost', float('inf')):
                    memory['best_cost'] = cand['cost']
                    memory['best_seq'] = cand['seq'].copy()
                    memory['stagnation'] = 0
                else:
                    memory['stagnation'] = memory.get('stagnation', 0) + 1

            # Age increment for pool members
            for p in pool:
                p['age'] = p.get('age', 0) + 1

            # Periodic diversify / restart
            if memory.get('stagnation', 0) > max(50, self.num_jobs):
                pool = self.restart_and_recombine(elite, pool_size)
                memory['stagnation'] = 0

        # Return best found sequence
        best_seq = memory.get('best_seq', None)
        if best_seq is None:
            # fallback: best in pool
            best = min(pool, key=lambda x: x['cost'])
            best_seq = best['seq']
        return list(map(int, best_seq.tolist()))

# Your new function
def evaluate_makespan(self, seq: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """
    Alternative makespan evaluator for permutation flow-shop.
    Builds the completion time matrix C where
        C[i, j] = processing_time(seq[i], j) + max(C[i-1, j], C[i, j-1])
    and returns C[-1, -1]. Uses numpy indexing to extract the sequence rows
    and a simple double loop to fill the DP table.
    """
    # Handle trivial/empty cases
    # If sequence is empty or no machines, makespan is zero
    try:
        seq_arr = np.asarray(seq, dtype=int)
    except Exception:
        seq_arr = np.array(list(seq), dtype=int)

    k = seq_arr.size
    if k == 0 or getattr(self, "num_machines", 0) == 0:
        return 0.0

    proc_times = self.processing_times  # numpy array shape (num_jobs, num_machines)
    M = int(self.num_machines)

    # Extract only the rows for the given sequence (shape: k x M)
    # This also converts possible numpy scalar types to standard numpy array entries
    job_rows = proc_times[seq_arr]

    # Completion time DP table: C[i, j] is completion time of i-th job in seq on machine j
    C = np.zeros((k, M), dtype=float)

    # Fill first cell
    C[0, 0] = float(job_rows[0, 0])

    # First job across machines (row 0) is cumulative sum
    for j in range(1, M):
        C[0, j] = C[0, j - 1] + float(job_rows[0, j])

    # Remaining jobs
    for i in range(1, k):
        # First machine for job i: previous job completion on machine 0 plus its processing time
        C[i, 0] = C[i - 1, 0] + float(job_rows[i, 0])
        for j in range(1, M):
            # job_rows[i, j] is the processing time for seq[i] on machine j
            pj = float(job_rows[i, j])
            # machine j becomes free at C[i-1, j] (previous job) and job i arrives at C[i, j-1]
            # so start = max(C[i-1, j], C[i, j-1])
            prev_start = C[i - 1, j]
            left = C[i, j - 1]
            if prev_start > left:
                start = prev_start
            else:
                start = left
            C[i, j] = start + pj

    return float(C[-1, -1])

procedure ADIC(problem, time_limit, params)              // Adaptive Decomposition with Interface Consensus
  model ← EncodeProblem(problem)                         // unified representation + interface variable schema
  interfaces ← InitInterfaceVariables(model)             // boundary orderings, loads, adjacency, dual multipliers
  partitions ← InitialPartition(model, interfaces, params)// spatial/clustering or job-subset decomposition
  best ← null; start ← now()
  while not Terminate(start, time_limit, params) do
    subsolutions ← ∅
    for each part in partitions do
      submodel ← BuildSubproblem(model, part, interfaces[part])            // fix interface ports as soft constraints
      subsol ← SolveSubproblemExactly(submodel, params.subsolver_time)    // use DP/MIP/TSP exact solver per subproblem
      subsolutions.add(subsol)
    end for
    consensus ← CoordinateInterfaces(subsolutions, interfaces)            // ADMM / Lagrangian consensus to reconcile boundaries
    candidate ← MergeSubsolutions(subsolutions, consensus)                // stitch with minimal interface penalty
    candidate ← RepairAndValidate(candidate, model)                       // global constraint fixes (capacities, permutations, precedences)
    if Evaluate(candidate, model) < Evaluate(best, model) then best ← candidate
    interfaces ← UpdateInterfaceVariables(interfaces, subsolutions, consensus, params) // update duals, reweight ports
    partitions ← AdaptiveRepartition(model, interfaces, subsolutions, params)         // split/merge to focus computation
  end while
  return DecodeSolution(best, model)
